title: Every Way to Bracket
statement: A math teacher writes an expression of whole numbers and the operators `+`, `-`, `*` with no brackets, such as `2*3-4*5`. Students may add brackets in any valid way to choose the order of operations. Return every result the class can get, one entry per way of bracketing (results can repeat), sorted from smallest to largest.
constraints: There is at least one number; operators sit between numbers

answerKey.pattern: Divide and conquer: split at each operator, combine every left result with every right result
keyPoints: Base case: an expression with no operator is a single number
For each operator, solve the left part and the right part recursively
Combine every left result with every right result using that operator
Collect the results from all split points, then sort
answerKey.timeComplexity: Grows quickly with the number of operators (Catalan numbers); fine for 9 operators
answerKey.spaceComplexity: Proportional to the number of results
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Remembering results for each substring speeds up longer expressions

hints: The last operation done must be one of the operators. Which parts does it split the expression into?
Solve each side the same way, which gives a list of possible values for each side.
For every split, combine each left value with each right value, add them all to one list, and sort it.
